Docket No. 21-0436 

ORDER NO. 9877 
SUSPENDING PROCEDURAL DEADLINES 
PENDING CONSIDERATION OF SETTLEMENT 
WHEREAS, on June 23, 2021, the Commission entered Order No. 9831, which (a) 
appointed the undersigned to serve as Hearing Examiner for this Docket, and (b) adopted a 
procedural schedule related to proceedings in this Docket; 
WHEREAS, on August 3, 2021, upon the joint request of Applicants, Veolia Environment 
S.A., Veolia North America, Inc., SUEZ S.A., and SUEZ Water Delaware Inc. (collectively the 
“Joint Applicants”), Commission Staff (“Staff”), and the Division of the Public Advocate 
(“DPA”), the undersigned Hearing Examiner entered Order No. 9852, extending certain deadlines 
in the case in order to allow time for the parties to engage in settlement discussions as contemplated 
by Order No. 9831; 
WHEREAS, on August 18, 2021, upon the joint request of the Joint Applicants, 
Commission Staff and the DPA, the undersigned Hearing Examiner entered Order No. 9870, 
further extending certain deadlines; 
WHEREAS, by email message sent to the Hearing Examiner on August 27, 2021, counsel 
for the Joint Applicants advised that the parties remained actively engaged in settlement 

2 

discussions and anticipated that they were close to a reaching a resolution of this matter by 
settlement, and requested, on behalf of the Joint Applicants, Staff and the DPA, that the deadlines 
in the schedule be suspended while the parties and their counsel attempted to finalize an agreement 
in principle to settle and resolve this matter; 
WHEREAS, counsel for the Joint Applicants, Staff and the DPA all agree that the Hearing 
Examiner is authorized to suspend the deadlines in the schedule as requested, by virtue of the 
powers delegated to the Hearing Examiner in Paragraph 2 of Order No. 9831, and under Section 
1.9.2 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Commission, 26 Del. Admin. Code § 1001-
1.9.2; and 
WHEREAS, there is good cause to suspend the deadlines in Order No. 9831, to allow the 
parties time to finalize a settlement in principle that will resolve the issues raised in this docket, 

NOW, THEREFORE, this 31st day of August 2021, pursuant to the authority granted to 
me in PSC Order No. 9831, dated June 23, 2021, this Hearing Examiner, having considered the 
application of the Joint Applicants, Staff and DPA as described above, orders as follows: 
1. 
The joint request of the Joint Applicants, Staff and DPA to suspend all procedural 
deadlines in this proceeding is granted. 
2. 
Counsel for the parties shall promptly report to the Hearing Examiner when they 
have reached an agreement in principle to settle the issues presented in this Docket. 
3. 
If an agreement in principle to settle this matter is reached, the Joint Applicants 
intend to present the terms of the settlement for Commission approval through a Final Order at the 
October 6, 2021 public meeting. 

3 

4. 
If the parties are unable to reach an agreement in principle to settle this matter, 
counsel for the Joint Applicants, Staff and the DPA shall confer on a proposal to revise the schedule 
for presenting the Application to the Commission. 
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 

/s/ Glenn C. Kenton 
Glenn C. Kenton 
Hearing Examiner 

Dated: August 31, 2021

ORDER NO. 9841 

EXTENDING DEADLINE FOR INTERVENTION 

WHEREAS, on June 23, 2021, the Commission entered Order No. 9831, which (a) 
appointed the undersigned to serve as Hearing Examiner for this Docket, (b) adopted a procedural 
schedule related to proceedings in this Docket, and (c) approved a form of notice to be published 
in newspapers of general circulation; 
WHEREAS, Order No. 9831 authorizes the Hearing Examiner to grant or deny 
applications for intervention and determine appropriate forms of notice related to matters in this 
proceeding; 
WHEREAS, by email message sent to the Hearing Examiner on June 29, 2021, on behalf 
of Applicants, Veolia Environnement S.A., Veolia North America, Inc., SUEZ S.A., and Suez 
Water Delaware Inc. (collectively the “Joint Applicants”), counsel for the Joint Applicants pointed 
out an anomaly in the schedule, in that Order No. 9831 contemplates publication of the notice in 
newspapers of general circulation on July 11, 2021, but sets a deadline for intervention four days 

2 

before publication, as applications for intervention are required to be made on or before July 7, 
2021; 
WHEREAS, in order to address the issue with the schedule noted above, counsel for the 
Joint Applicants propose that (a) the intervention deadline for this Docket be extended to July 14, 
2021, and (b) that the notice published on July 11, 2021 reflect the extended intervention deadline 
of July 14, 2021; 
WHEREAS, counsel for Commission Staff and counsel for the Division of the Public 
Advocate (the “DPA”) concur in the request of the Joint Applicants to adjust the intervention 
deadline by moving it back one week; 
WHEREAS, counsel for the Joint Applicants, Commission Staff and the DPA all agree 
that the Hearing Examiner is authorized to extend the intervention deadline as requested, by virtue 
of the powers delegated to the Hearing Examiner in Paragraph 2 of Order No. 9831, and under 
Section 2.9.4 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Commission, 26 Del. Admin Code § 
1001-2.9.4; 
WHEREAS, no party objects to the extension of the deadline to intervene as proposed by 
the Joint Applicants and the extension of the deadline will not prejudice Commission Staff, the 
DPA, or any potential intervenor; and 
WHEREAS, there is good cause to extend the intervention deadline so that interested 
parties who become aware of this Docket through publication of the notice have an opportunity to 
timely intervene in the proceeding, 

3 

NOW, THEREFORE, this 1st day of July, 2021, pursuant to the authority granted to me in 
PSC Order No. 9831, dated June 23, 2021, this Hearing Examiner having considered the 
application of the Joint Applicants as described above: 
1. 
The Joint Applicants’ request to extend the intervention deadline to July 14, 2021 
is approved, and the deadline for interested parties to intervene in this Docket is extended to July 
14, 2021. 
2. 
The notice to be published on July 11, 2021, pursuant to Paragraph 3 of Order No. 
9831, will provide the extended intervention deadline of July 14, 2021. 
3. 
All other dates and deadlines for this Docket shall remain as set forth in Order No. 
9831 and Exhibit A thereto. 
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
s/s Glenn C. Kenton 
Glenn C. Kenton 
Hearing Examiner

pursuant to Order No. 10439, Delmarva published on May 14, 2024, in the

at which Staff and Delmarva presented witnesses who testified that the 2024 SOS-PCA-RARM

text:
BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE
IN THE MATTER OF REQUEST FOR APPROVAL 
)

2025 STANDARD OFFER SERVICE RATES, )

ORDER NO. 10439
AND NOW, 
this U' day of May 2024, the Delaware Public Service Commission
("Commission") determines and orders the following:
WHEREAS, on March 27, 2024, Delmarva Power & Light Company
("Delmarva") submitted revised electric tariffs and requested approval of the 2024
Standard Offer Service ("SOS") Rates, Procurement Cost Adjustment ("PCA"), and
Reasonable Allowance for a Retail Margin ("RARM") 
(collectively, the "2024 SOS-PCA-
RARM Filing").' The 2024 SOS-PCA-RARM Filing included revised tariff sheets 39 to
47, 50, 112, and 114. Additionally, Delmarva filed workpapers supporting the proposed
tariff changes as well as the monthly bill impact information that showed a proposed
increase of approximately $2.34 (a 1.65% change) for a typical residential (Non-Space
Heating) customer using 811 kWh on an annual average basis; and
^ Delmarva made its 2024 SOS-PCA-RARM filing pursuant to the provisions of the
Second Amended Settlement approved by the Commission on December 22, 2021,
by Order No. 9933 in Docket Nos. 09-9 and 04-391. The Second Amended
Settlement superseded settlements from 2005 (approved by Order No. 6746 (Oct.
11, 2005), in Docket No. 04-391) and 2009 (approved by Order No. 7703 (Dec. 22,
2009) in Docket No. 09-9). See Order No. 9933 for more details regarding the
history of the changes to the SOS-PCA-RARM process.

PSC Docket No. 24-0365, Order No. 10439 Cont'd
WHEREAS, 
according to the 2024 SOS-PCA-RARM Filing, the RARM rate for
fixed price customers decreased by 34.34%^ from the RARM rate currently in effect.
Delmarva included workpapers supporting the results of the RARM factor on an actual
basis for the reporting year ending December 31, 2023, and on an estimated basis for the
rate effective period. The RARM component will be subject to formal discovery; and
WHEREAS, 
on November 6, 2023 and January 29,2024, Delmarva conducted its
nineteenth annual SOS procurement for supply contracts commencing on June 1, 2024.^
The procurement, which was conducted in two "tranches," secured two-year supply
contracts for 50% of the residential and small commercial SOS load and one-year contracts
for 100% of the load for other "fixed price" types of service. The Liberty Consulting
Group, Inc ("Liberty"), along with Staff, observed and evaluated the supply procurement
in each tranche; and
WHEREAS, 
at the Commission's February 21, 2024 meeting. Liberty presented
its final report dated February 21, 2024, which discussed the details of each procurement
and the successful bids for the 2024 SOS RFP. The 2024 SOS-PCA-RARM Filing reflects
the results of the successful bids, as well as the PCA and RARM; 
and
^ The RARM factor is included in the monthly bill impact increase of approximately $2.34 (a 1.65%
change).
^ By Order No. 7461 (Oct. 7, 2008) in Docket No. 04-391, the Commission approved Delmarva's
request to utilize in its annual SOS proeurement a reverse auction process conducted by World
Energy Solutions Inc. Effective January 5,2015, EnerNOC acquired World Energy Solutions Inc.;
on August 7, 2017, Enel Green Power North America acquired EnerNOC; on October 1, 2018,
EnerNOC was rebranded to Enel X, which is the current auction platform name.
2

PSC Docket No. 24-0365, Order No. 10439 Cont'd
WHEREAS, 
as discussed in its report. Liberty found that the auction resulted in
bids that were consistent with expectations based on market conditions; and
WHEREAS, Commission Staff ("Staff) has begun its review of the 2024
SOS-PCA-RARM Filing. At this time, and pending further review, Staff recommends
that the Commission approve Delmarva's proposed rate changes on a temporary basis,
subject to refund with interest effective with usage on and after June 1, 2024, and with the
appropriate public notice, and further recommends that the Commission accept Liberty's
final report as presented on February 21, 2024, and that the revised rates and revised tariff
provisions set forth in the 2024 SOS-PCA-RARM Filing, as amended, be permitted to take
effect on a temporary basis with usage on and after June 1, 2024;
NOW, 
THEREFORE, 
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED BY THE AFFIRMATIVE
VOTE OF NOT FEWER THAN THREE COMMISSIONERS:
1. 
The "Technical Consultant's Final Report To the Delaware Public Service
Commission - Delmarva Power & Light's 2024 Request for Proposals for Full
Requirements Wholesale Electric Supply for Standard Offer Service," dated February 21,
2024, as prepared and given to the Commission by Liberty, is hereby accepted.
2. 
Pursuant to 26 Del. C. § 306(a)(1), the Commission hereby approves on a
temporary basis, effective with usage on and after June 1, 2024, the 2024 SOS-PCA-
RARM Filing, including the revised rates and revised tariff sheets. Such rates shall be
subject to refund, with interest, if the Commission determines in a final order that such
rates are, in whole or in part, unjust or unreasonable.

PSC Docket No. 24-0365, Order No. 10439 Cont'd
3. 
Delmarva shall publish the form of notice attached as Exhibit "A" in the
following newspapers, on the designated dates, in two-column format outlined in black:
On or before May 20, 2024 - The News Journal:
On or before May 20, 2024 - Delaware State News; and
On or before May 20, 2024 - Cape Gazette.
Delmarva shall cause the affidavits of publication of the above notices to be filed in this
docket within two weeks of becoming available.
4. 
Interested persons may file petitions for intervention, written comments, or
objections to the proposed rates and tariff changes on or before June 24, 2024. If material
written comments or objections are filed, or if Staff recommends changes to the proposed
rates or tariff revisions temporarily approved by this Order, the Commission will
determine, by fiirther Order, the course of any further proceedings. If material written
comments or objections are not filed and Staff recommends final approval of the rates and
revised tariff sheets, then the Commission may enter a final order at a duly-noticed public
hearing.
5. 
Delmarva is hereby notified that it will be charged the costs of this
proceeding under 26 De/. C. § 114(b)(1).
6. 
The Commission reserves the jurisdiction and authority to enter such further
Orders in this matter as may be deemed necessary or proper.

TO: ALL CUSTOMERS OF DELMARVA POWER & LIGHT COMPANY

On March 27, 2024, Delmarva Power & Light Company ("Delmarva" or the
"Company") filed with the Delaware Public Service Commission (the "Commission") an
application requesting changes to its Electric Tariff related to its Standard Offer Supply
("SOS") service offerings including:
)
(a) 
Changes in the rates for fixed price SOS to reflect the bid
prices from the recent "fixed price" SOS wholesale procurement process;
(b) 
Revision of the Procurement Cost Adjustment factors
applicable to both fixed price SOS and hourly price (SOS and returning
customer) services; and

(c) Revision of the Reasonable Allowance for Retail Margin
applicable to both fixed price SOS and Hourly Prices (SOS and returning
customer) services.
According to the Company's calculations, not including the Qualified Fuel Cell
Provider Project ("Bloom") or Renewable Portfolio Standards ("RPS") Charge, the
monthly bill for a residential customer using 811 kWh on an annual average basis will
increase by approximately $2.34 (a 1.65% change).
On May 1, 2024, in PSC Order No. 10439, the Commission allowed the proposed
rates and tariff changes, as amended, to go into effect with usage on or after June 1, 2024,
on a temporary basis, but subject to refund with interest if the Commission later determines
in a final order that such rates and charges are incorrect, unjust, or unreasonable.
Interested persons may file written comments or objections to the proposed rates
and tariff changes on or before June 24, 2024. If you wish to formally participate as a
party in this matter, with the right to present evidence and be represented by counsel, you
must file with the Commission a written petition asking for leave to intervene in accordance
with the requirements of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (26 Del.

ORDER NO. 11019
AND NOW, this 20ft day of May 2026, the Delaware Public Service Commission
('oCommission") determines and orders the following:
WHEREAS, on August 17, 2017, Delmarva Power and Light Company (Delmarva" or
the "Company") filed an application ("Docket 17-0977") for an increase in electric distribution
rates; and
WHEREAS' on August 21, 2018, the Delaware Public Service Commission (the
"Commission") adopted Order No. 9248 in Docket No. 17-0977, which approved a settlement
agreement (the "settlement Agreement") entered into by all parties in Docket 17-0977; and
WHEREAS, Section II.1.(c) of the Settlement Agreemdnt addressed the impact of the Tax
Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA") and the process for how the Company's Excess Deferred
Income Taxes ("EDIT") would be flowed back to customers; specifically, $44.3 million of non-
protected property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a six-year amortization period, and
$20.8 million of non-protected non-property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a five-year
amortization period; I and
t $62.5 million and $29.3 million respectively when grossed up by the revenue conversion factor of 1.40926

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 11019 Cont'd
WHEREAS' on March 31,2026, Delmarva filed an application (the "Application") to
modiff its electric Rider "EDIT" Excess Defened Income Tax Credit ("Rider EDIT"); and
WHEREAS, Delmarva intends to reset to zero ($0.000000) certain Rider EDIT service
classifications whose EDIT liability balances have been fully credited to the respective customers;
and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Section II.l.(c)(vii) of the Settlement Agreement, because the
amounts due to the customers in each service classification could not be calculated precisely at the
time of the Settlement Agreement, the parties agreed that any amounts paid to customers in excess
of the total EDIT balance will be recorded as a regulatory asset with a retum at the Company's
Commission authorized rate of return to be recovered in the Company's subsequent rate case; and
WHEREAS, Delmarva has requested similar treatment to that received in PSC Order No.
10135, issued December 14,2022, PSC Order No. 10179, issued February 22,2023, PSC Order
No. 10282, issued August 23,2023,PSC OrderNo. 10338, issuedNovember 29,2023,PSC Order
No. 10518, issued August 21, 2024, and PSC Order No. 10941, issued January 28,2026, that
instead of carrying a regulatory asset balance for the five-year EDIT credits, any regulatory asset
balance be transferred to the respective six-year regulatory liability balance to reduce the
remaining liability if that balance still has a credit; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule 1 of the Application, the General Service - Water Heating
("GS-WH") five-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of
May 2026. The Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective June l, 2026; and
2

PSC Docket No. 17-0917, Order No. 11019 Cont'd
WHEREAS, the Company requests authority to transfer any regulatory asset balance for
the GS-WH five-year EDIT credit to the respective six-year EDIT liability balance, thus reducing
the respective six-year EDIT liability balance; and
WHEREAS, Staff submitted a memorandum to the Commission recommending that the
five-year EDIT credit for the GS-WH rate class be set to zero effective June 1, 2026, and that any
regulatory asset balance for this rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability
balance;
NOW, THEREFORE,IT IS HEREBY ORDERED BY THE AFFIRMATIVE
VOTE OF NOT F'EWER THAN THREE COMMISSIONERS:
1. 
That the five-year EDIT credit for the GS-WH rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective June 1, 2026.
2. 
That any regulatory asset balance from the five-year EDIT credit for the GS-WH
rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability.
3. 
Delmarva is hereby notified that it will be assessed the costs of this proceeding
pursuant to 26 Del. C. $ 114(b).
4. 
The Commission reserves the jurisdiction and authority to enter such further orders
in this matter as may be deemed necessary or proper.

caption: IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF DELMARVA POWER & LIGHT COMPANY FOR AN INCREASE IN ELECTRIC BASE RATES AND MISCELLANEOUS TARIFF CHANGES (FILED AUGUST 17, 2017).
title: DE PSC Docket 17-0977 — Order No. 10518
text:
BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE
IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF
DELMARVA POWER AND LIGHT COMPANY
FOR AN INCREASE IN ELECTRIC BASE
RATES AND MISCELLANEOUS TARIFF
CHANGES
(FILED AUGUST 17, 2017)
PSC DOCKET NO. 17-0977
ORDER NO. 10518
AND NOW, 
this 2U' day of August 2024, the Delaware Public Service Commission
("Commission") determines and orders the following:
WHEREAS, on August 17, 2017, Delmarva Power and Light Company (Delmarva" or
the "Company") filed an application ("Docket 17-0977") for an increase in electric distribution
rates; and
WHEREAS, on August 21, 2018, the Delaware Public Service Commission (the
"Commission") adopted Order No. 9248 in Docket No. 17-0977, which approved a settlement
agreement (the "Settlement Agreement") entered into by all parties in Docket 17-0977; and
WHEREAS, 
Section II. I .(c) of the Settlement Agreement addressed the impact of the Tax
Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA") and the process for how the Company's Excess Deferred
Income Taxes ("EDIT") would be flowed hack to customers; specifically, $44.3 million of non
protected property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a six-year amortization period, and
$20.8 million of non-protected non-property related EDIT was to he flowed hack using a five-year
amortization period;' and
' 
$62.5 million and $29.3 million respectively when grossed up by the revenue conversion factor of 1.40926.

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10518 Cont'd
WHEREAS, on June 25, 2024, Delmarva filed an application (the "Application") to
modify its electric Rider "EDIT" Excess Deferred Income Tax Credit ("Rider EDIT"); and
WHEREAS, Delmarva intends to reset to zero ($0.000000) certain Rider EDIT service
elassifications whose EDIT liability balanees have been fully credited to the respective customers;
and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Section II.l.(c)(vii) of the Settlement Agreement, because the
amounts due to the customers in each service elassification could not be calculated precisely at the
time of the Settlement Agreement, the parties agreed that any amounts paid to customers in excess
of the total EDIT balance will be recorded as a regulatory asset with a return at the Company's
Commission authorized rate of return to be recovered in the Company's subsequent rate case; and
WHEREAS, 
Delmarva has requested similar treatment to that received in PSC Order No.
10135, issued December 14, 2022, PSC Order No. 10179, issued February 22, 2023, PSC Order
No. 10282, issued August 23, 2023, and PSC Order No. 10338, issued November 29, 2023, that
instead of carrying a regulatory asset balance for the five-year EDIT credits, any regulatory asset
balance be transferred to the respective six-year regulatory liability balance to reduce the
remaining liability if that balanee still has a credit; and
WHEREAS, 
per Schedule 1 of the Application, the General Service Primary ("GSP") five-
year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully eredited to the rate class by end of August 2024. The
Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate elass to zero effective September 1,
2024; and
WHEREAS, 
per Schedule 1 of the Application, the Medium General Service - Secondary
("MGS-S") five-year EDIT balanee is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10518 Cont'd
September 2024. The Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective October 1, 2024; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule 1 of the Application, the Outdoor Recreational Lighting
("ORL") six-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of
November 2024. The Company intends to set the six-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective December 1, 2024; and
WHEREAS, 
the Company requests authority to transfer any regulatory asset balances for
the GSP and MGS-S five-year EDIT credits to the respective six-year EDIT liability balances, thus
reducing the respective six-year EDIT liability balances; and
WHEREAS, Staff submitted a memorandum to the Commission recommending that 1)
the five-year EDIT credits for the GSP and MGS-S rate classes be set to zero effective September
1, 2024, and October 1, 2024, respectively, and that any regulatory asset balances for these two
rate classes be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability balances; and 2) the six-year
EDIT credit for the ORL rate class be set to zero effective December 1, 2024, and any regulatory
asset balance for this rate class be addressed in the Company's next rate case;
NOW, 
THEREFORE, 
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED BY THE AFFIRMATIVE
VOTE OF NOT FEWER THAN THREE COMMISSIONERS:
1. 
That the five-year EDIT credit for the GSP rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective September 1, 2024.
2. 
That any regulatory asset balance from the five-year EDIT credit for the GSP rate
class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability.
3. 
That the five-year EDIT credit for the MGS-S rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective October 1, 2024.

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10518 Cont'd
4. 
That any regulatory asset balance from the five-year EDIT credit for the MGS-S
rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability.
5. 
That the six-year EDIT credit for the ORE rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective December 1, 2024
6. 
That any regulatory asset balances resulting from the six-year EDIT credit for the
ORE rate class will be addressed in Delmarva's next rate case.
7. 
Delmarva is hereby notified that it will be assessed the costs of this proceeding
pursuant to 26 Del. C. § 114(b).
8. 
The Commission reserves the jurisdiction and authority to enter such further orders
in this matter as may be deemed necessary or proper.
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
